description: Dancik (1994) and Lueker (2009) used DFA-based Markov chains to produce both lower and upper bounds on gamma_2. Heineman et al. (2024) improved this with parallelization and memory optimization, achieving 0.792665992. The key opportunity is designing new automata with richer state spaces that exploit structural properties of optimal LCS alignments.
mathematical_formalization: DFA M with state space Q reads pairs (x_i, y_j). Stationary distribution pi of induced Markov chain gives rate r(M) = sum_q pi(q) * p_match(q). Then gamma_2 >= r(M). Dual automaton gives upper bounds.
implementation_hypothesis: Design automaton with state = (buffer of h chars from X, buffer of h chars from Y, offset mod k). For h=16, use distributed computation. Target lower bound > 0.7927.
experiment_seed: Reproduce h=15 result (0.792665992). Try h=16 with optimized code. Estimate runtime for marginal improvement.
